# Ida Ashdown

## Appearance

Ida is a little girl with slanted, deep dark-blue eyes that often bear a yearning or piteous expression. Her pitch-black hair is kept in plaits and brushed to a satiny smoothness without any wild curls. Though she lacks conventional beauty, her attire includes a discolored tam that serves as her finest headwear.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 CHAPTER IX. ## Personality

Ida is an endearing, ten-year-old girl with a timid and gentle nature who detests conflict and experiences deep sympathy for others. She genuinely enjoys prayer and secretly dreams of taking music lessons, though she prefers to remain at home. Additionally, she harbors a fear of having a stepmother, believing that the role alters a person's demeanor.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P51](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0051), [v5 CHAPTER VIII. ## History

Ida Ashdown's mother died when Ida was six years old, and her family lived in [Juneford](../codex/places.md#juneford) before moving to [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. [Agnes](../codex/places.md#agnes). After settling in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), Ida and her siblings quickly befriended the local [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) children over a meal at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). When the siblings discovered a runaway girl named [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) hiding in an old barn, Ida comforted Mary in the parsonage garret, listening to her fears before they reconciled. Upon learning of the death of Mary's former guardian, Ida promised to pray that Mary could remain in the area, and she later personally visited Miss Winifred to ask her to take the girl in, leading to Mary's adoption. When Mary later mentioned rumors that Ida's father might remarry, Ida was left frightened and tearful.

After mixing up their calendar days while their father was away, Ida and her sister [Grace](../character/grace.md) accidentally sparked a scandal by cleaning house and beating carpets in the cemetery on a Sunday. Following this and other missteps, the siblings joined Kit Carrow's suggested [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) to regulate their behavior, though Ida remained anxious about rumors regarding a stepmother. When the club chose to fast on a Sunday to punish themselves for an disruptive graveyard song, a weakened Ida fainted during the church service and had to be revived by Doctor [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) and Mrs. Elder Clow. On another occasion, while returning from [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) at night, Ida and her siblings were terrified by what they believed to be a ghost in a garden, fleeing to [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) where [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) helped calm them down. Seeking happiness for her father, Ida eventually visited [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to ask her to marry him, promising to be well-behaved, and successfully carried a letter back to her father that led toward their engagement.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P20](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0020), [v5 CHAPTER IV. ## Quotes

> "Yet it was placed within her heart by God to adopt you. Had He not done so, no amount of my urging her would have achieved anything."
>
> — Ida Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER IX. IDA INTERVENES P69](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0069)

> “He would go to just as much effort on your behalf, Mary, I am certain,” Ida declared. “The identity of your parents is irrelevant. Simply make your request to Him—and I shall do so as well.”
>
> — Ida Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P111](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0111)

> “Oh, Mary,” uttered Ida, sliding a gentle arm across Mary’s rigid back, “do not speak in such a way. I really like you a great deal. And you cause me to feel terribly.”
>
> — Ida Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P124](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0124)

> "Oh, no, no, Mary. I feel certain that praying to the devil couldn’t be proper. Furthermore, it would be useless since he is evil. Doing so might rile him up, making him even worse."
>
> — Ida Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER IX. IDA INTERVENES P75](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0075)

> "Should you become lonely, simply gaze toward our window and keep in mind that I am in there, awake, and contemplating you. Will that not offer a bit of companionship?"
>
> — Ida Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER XXXI. RUPERT DOES PENANCE P16](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0016)

[Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) is Ida Ashdown's aunt who manages household affairs, though their home life can be chaotic.
